transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jenna Morales (Redwood SE), Emily Parker (Westlake Bank - Head of AI), Derek Lin (Infra Lead), Maya Singh (CISO)

Auto-generated Summary (may be rough):
Westlake Bank is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for production inference. Primary concerns: reserved GPU sizing, isolation / VPC and data residency, burst/overflow strategy, scaling and autoscale policy, benchmarking latency and cost per token. Security team needs SOC2 + KMS details, network diagrams, and SLA commitments. Next step to send pricing, architecture docs, and schedule a bench run.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um this is Samir from Redwood, i'm the AE on this. Jenna is our systems eng joining. how's everyone doing?
[00:05] Emily: Good thanks, Emily here. we, uh, really want to get into the dedicated conversation, last week we did a quick hosted POC and saw decent perf but we need isolation and predictable throughput for the product.
[00:12] Jenna: cool, can you describe the workload? is it 1:1 chat, batched inference, embeddings, mix?
[00:18] Emily: mostly chat and summarization, about 40k users active, peak concurrency estimates around 1200 concurrent requests, average prompt length maybe 600 tokens, summaries shorter. we also have nightly batch jobs that generate embeddings for search, those can be scheduled.
[00:31] Derek: from infra side, we're on AWS us-east-1, we run in a VPC with strict egress rules. For Dedicated we need private connectivity options, ideally VPC peering or Transit Gateway, and we need to keep logs in our S3 buckets. no public internet egress for customer data.
[00:45] Maya: security perspective, we require SOC2 Type II, SSO via SAML, RBAC, and key management with our KMS/HSM. also data residency for EU customers is a later ask.
[00:53] Samir: great, all that aligns with other Dedicated customers. Quick overview: Redwood Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool with configurable autoscaling and burst to hosted for overflow. you can pin model versions, we support VPC peering and private link. for KMS we integrate with customer K M S and can do envelope encryption.
[01:10] Emily: when you say burst to hosted, is that automatic? how does billing work if some requests go to hosted?
[01:16] Jenna: it's policy based. you can set quota thresholds and latency SLOs. when Dedicated capacity is saturated we can optionally route to a hosted fallback or queue; billing is split - reserved capacity charged monthly and burst usage billed at a defined per-token or per-instance rate. i'll share exact numbers after the call.
[01:28] Derek: capacity planning question: we think we'll need 4 GPUs reserved initially, maybe A100s, to meet tail latency at our concurrency. do you have sizing guidance?
[01:34] Jenna: yes, generally for 600-token median sequences with chat model variants, 1 A100 -> ~80-120 concurrent light chat sessions depending on batching. tail latency and KV cache behaviors mean we often recommend starting with 4 nodes for 1k concurrency and then autoscale with policies. but we should run a benchmark with your prompt set for accurate guidance.
[01:50] Emily: can you do burst capacity instantaneous? like if we suddenly get a spike to 2k conc?
[01:55] Samir: bursting to hosted is near-instant from a routing perspective but you will see higher latency and different cost characteristics. for very short spikes we can also provision ephemeral burst capacity in Dedicated regionally but that usually requires a separate contract for buffer capacity.
[02:07] Maya: network and audit: we need audit logs, per-request tracing, and token-level cost visibility for billing. do you store prompts or model outputs? what's retention?
[02:16] Jenna: customers choose retention policies. for Dedicated we offer options: no retention, short-term retention for debugging, or retention with encryption under your K M S. audit logs can be shipped to your S3/CloudWatch; per-request tracing is supported via our tracing hooks.
[02:30] Derek: what's the rollback story? if a model rollout causes regressions, can we fallback to previous model easily?
[02:35] Samir: yes rollouts are canary/A B and automatic fallback. you can pin versions per route. we've seen that be critical for production usages.
[02:42] Emily: security: can we bring our own key for model encryption?
[02:45] Jenna: yes BYOK with the K M S integration, we support rotating keys and customer-managed HSM for Private deployments; Dedicated can be integrated with your KMS.
[02:53] Derek: what about software updates/maintenance windows? we can't have noisy service restarts during our business hours.
[02:59] Jenna: maintenance windows are configurable. Dedicated gives you control over patch windows, and hot patches are orchestrated to avoid full pool downtime. we'll provide an SLA and maintenance schedule.
[03:09] Emily: we also need deterministic latency under 200ms p95 for short prompts - is that realistic?
[03:15] Jenna: for short prompts on A100s with optimized kernels and proper batching, p95 sub-200ms is achievable, but it depends on KV cache warm state and model variant. if you need strict SLOs we can recommend pinned model flavors and reserved capacity to reduce variability.
[03:29] Samir: can you tell us about timeline and stakeholders? are you aiming to be in prod by Q2?
[03:34] Emily: timeline is end of Q2 for a soft launch. stakeholders include product, infra, security, and compliance. budget decision lives with infra procurement team and finance.
[03:43] Derek: procurement will need contract terms, minimum commit and burst rates, and exit/termination terms. also curious on pricing model for reserved allocation vs burst.
[03:52] Samir: typical reserved commit is monthly or annual; we can do 12-month with discounts. burst is metered. i'll include a sample pricing sheet showing per-GPU reserved price and burst rate per token.
[03:59] Maya: can you provide your SOC2 report and a network diagram? we need to present to our auditors.
[04:05] Samir: yes we'll share the compliance pack - SOC2, ISO summary, and the Dedicated architecture diagram. Jenna will attach the benchmark spreadsheet.
[04:12] Emily: one technical question - model quantization and performance: do you support int8 or 4-bit quant? that affects throughput and cost.
[04:19] Jenna: our runtime supports quantized variants and we recommend specific quantization profiles for certain models. caveat: quality regressions can occur; Redwood Optimize offers recommendations and eval tooling to track regressions against your prompt set.
[04:31] Derek: on private deployments for regulated data, is there an on-prem option?
[04:35] Samir: yes Redwood Private is available - full onprem or VPC-hosted control plane. that tends to be enterprise licensing with additional support fees.
[04:42] Emily: what's the minimal POC we can run? maybe a 2-week bench with 1-2 reserved GPUs and a burst to hosted so we can see real latencies and cost?
[04:49] Jenna: that's reasonable. POC typically includes a benchmark run with your prompts, latency and cost metrics, and a short integration window. we can scope a 2-week POC with 2 A100s and optional burst.
[04:58] Maya: last sec question: how do you handle data deletion requests and audit trails?
[05:02] Jenna: we support data deletion flows, retention policies, and can provide audit trails. for Dedicated with no retention we won't store payloads. if retention is enabled we encrypt and can delete on request.
[05:12] Samir: ok let's recap next steps: i'll send pricing and contract outline; Jenna will share architecture and benchmarks; Maya will send compliance questions. can we aim to reconvene next Tuesday?
[05:20] Emily: yes next tues works for a deeper POC scoping call. thanks all.
[05:25] Derek: thanks.
[05:26] Jenna: thanks everyone, i'll follow up with the docs.
[05:30] Maya: bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on audio quality: transcription had a few misheard acronyms (K M S sometimes broken out), occasional filler words preserved.
